goal: T-011: Worktree contract parity + proposal refresh
refresh_summary: Revalidated the bounded external evidence set for BL-065. The stored worktree conclusions still hold: the official git-worktree manual now shows its last update in 2.54.0 on 2026-04-20, while git-sparse-checkout remains last updated in 2.52.0 with 2.53.0 reporting no changes.
limitations: Official Git documentation is treated as normative for worktree behavior as observed on 2026-04-22.
Academic multi-agent sources are directional architecture input, not hard product requirements.
Repo-local findings describe current Azoth behavior in this repository snapshot and may age as implementation lands.

questions.question: Can this worktree-upgrade research capsule be reused for the next worktree planning slice?
What is implemented now versus planned next for the T-011 worktree contract parity slice?

sources.title: git-worktree manual
sources.published_context: Official Git documentation (manual last updated in 2.54.0 on 2026-04-20 as observed on 2026-04-22)
findings: The current git-worktree manual still frames linked worktrees as explicit lifecycle objects created with `git worktree add` and cleaned up with `git worktree remove`.
Per-worktree configuration support (`extensions.worktreeConfig`) reinforces keeping temporary integration state isolated.

sources.title: git-sparse-checkout manual
sources.published_context: Official Git documentation (manual last updated in 2.52.0 on 2025-11-17; 2.53.0 reports no changes, as observed on 2026-04-22)
findings: The current sparse-checkout manual explicitly says the `set` subcommand upgrades the repository to worktree-specific config when needed so one worktree's sparsity changes do not alter another's.
Azoth can safely model sandbox integration state as ephemeral per-worktree state instead of canonical repo truth.

sources.title: A Survey on LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
findings: Role specialization is useful when coordination stays bounded and explicit.
Control-plane clarity matters as much as agent count.

sources.title: Rethinking the Value of Multi-Agent Workflow: A Strong Single Agent Baseline
findings: Multi-agent workflow should be justified against strong single-agent baselines.
Extra lanes should exist only when they add distinct evidence or independence.

sources.title: Understanding Agent Scaling in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems via Diversity
sources.published_context: ICLR 2026 AIMS workshop paper on OpenReview (modified 2026-03-30)
findings: Agent diversity matters more than raw agent count.
Bounded specialized lanes are preferable to unstructured swarm expansion.

sources.title: AEMA: Verifiable Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy and Controlled Agentic LLM Systems
sources.published_context: AAAI 2026 TrustAgent workshop poster on OpenReview (modified 2026-03-09)
findings: Evidence-backed evaluation and explicit reviewer independence improve trustworthiness.
Audit trails should survive beyond a single agent run.

repo_findings: scripts/worktree_sync.py currently implements producer refresh, dirty-target preflight, ready handoff queueing, and integrated marking.
The current command/playbook surface claims more integration behavior than the backend executes today.
Detached HEAD handling is inconsistent: command copy is permissive, backend validation is not.
Shared Azoth state files remain the main reconciliation risk for future integrate-run work.
The BL-065 refresh pass did not uncover a new external fact that changes the T-012/T-013/T-014 phased split; the existing staged follow-on remains the right decomposition.
